exact_statement: For every finite uniform-cube Boolean sign, two-coordinate queried block A and K>=4, let c_t=E(w_t^2/q_t-1)^2, C_A=sum q_t c_t, Gamma_A=sum q_t log2(1+c_t), and classify actual Boolean phases sign(w_t), sign(0)=1, into constant mass W0, nonconstant good mass Wg (c_t<=1/16) and nonconstant bad mass Wb. With S_A=-E D_K(physical child), D_K(f)+S_A+(K/2-2)Wg<=Gamma_A+log2(1+3*2^-K)W0+2Wb. An alternative upper bound is Gamma_A+psi_2(min(1,C_A))+2Wb, where psi_2(s)=h2(s)+s log2 3 up to s=3/4 and equals2 thereafter. Wb<=16C_A and C_A<=6I_A; hence for C_A<=3/4 the alternative is at most log2(1+C_A)+h2(C_A)+(log2 3+32)C_A, an O(C_A log(1/C_A)) modulus. On a least-essential-dimension FEI(K) violation these identities retain S_A>=0 and D_K>0 on every pair, without assuming an optimizer. The actual sign (-1)^((x1 xor x2)y) has singleton collisions0 and joint pair collision1, so no unconditional finite-constant comparison C_pair<=c(C_x1+C_x2) holds. No uniform paid pair or full FEI bound is claimed.
